A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LUDVIG and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Content can be matched across the revised methods, reordered sections, and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation, open-vocabulary localization, ablation, runtime, and qualitative results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original results on the retained benchmarks, including revised numerical outcomes and additional segmentation ablations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Normalized feature aggregation remains, but downstream diffusion substantially changes. v2 diffuses CLIP embeddings with no unary term and computes relevance after projection; v4 computes and refines per-Gaussian relevance using query-specific logistic unaries (Section 4.2, Appendix A.4). Foreground segmentation replaces direct rendering of diffusion weights with binarized-graph reachability and unary-weighted masks, and revises seed selection (Appendix A.3).

E1.justification: Both use NVOS, SPIn-NeRF, and LangSplat’s extended LERF evaluation for the same segmentation and localization tasks. The added component variants and qualitative cases do not establish a distinct task, population, or evaluation regime.

E2.justification: The named external comparators remain unchanged, including LERF and LangSplat in Table 3 and the retained segmentation baselines. v4 adds internal comparison methods for LERF segmentation: raw relevance, diffusion without SAM, and SAM without diffusion, compared with the combined method in Table 4.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 changes the reported LERF smoothing kernel from 11 to 5 and SAM mask averaging from 10 to 20 predictions, alongside revised threshold selection. The appendix runtime example changes image resolution from 480×640 to 724×986. Benchmark splits, principal metrics, and backbone choices remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds a four-condition LERF ablation testing SAM and graph diffusion separately and together (Table 4). Figure 10 and Appendix C.4.1 replace the earlier CLIP-feature PCA demonstration with segmentation case analyses. Table 5 also adds empirical profiling of feature generation, uplifting, scene-specific processing, query-specific processing, and segmentation.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three independent runs. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The increased number of SAM predictions concerns inference ensembling, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Primary and per-scene results change. DINOv2 SPIn-NeRF IoU changes from 92.8 to 93.8; Table 3 reports LERF localization accuracy of 85.1 versus 86.3, segmentation IoU of 61.3 versus 64.3, and runtime of 9 versus 10 minutes. Changes are not uniformly positive: Waldo segmentation falls from 67.7 to 58.5. These are revised-pipeline results, not isolated same-setting gains. New ablation and profiling entries further expand the results.

T1.justification: Equation (7) changes unary factors from P^(-1/2) to P^(1/2), and graph adjacency changes from one-sided nearest-neighbor membership to the union of both directions. These are substantive mathematical revisions. The normalized-aggregation equations and their preconditioned-gradient-step interpretation remain.

C1.justification: The learning-free uplifting and efficiency claims remain. Section 1 refocuses the CLIP contribution from embedding refinement for competitive localization to open-vocabulary segmentation, explicitly extending segmentation without SAM and highlighting the SAM-plus-diffusion combination. This adjusts the contribution’s scope within the existing research program.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 replaces general feature-coherence interpretations with detailed explanations of wrong-object selection, incomplete object coverage, neighboring-object leakage, and SAM–diffusion complementarity. Appendix B.1 adds an account of shared versus query-dependent costs. Conversely, Section 6 removes the explicit bandwidth-selection cost caveat, while retaining reconstruction limitations and documenting foreground tuning in Appendix A.3.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 substantially expand implementable details, including similarity scaling, graph thresholds, seed selection, logistic-regression regularization and class weighting, and fixed bandwidths. PCA eigenvalue weighting is newly documented. Table 5 supplies workload counts and detailed timings, and the first page adds a project-page pointer; its external contents are not assessed.

R1.justification: v4 adds an Otsu reference for thresholding already mentioned in v2 and explicitly contrasts its per-Gaussian relevance computation with LangSplat’s pixel-level computation (Appendix A.4.1). The broader related-work survey and positioning against optimization-based uplifting remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, contributions, graph explanation, and downstream-task descriptions. Appendix A.4 gains localization and segmentation subsections, runtime analysis precedes per-scene results, and terminology and grammar are refined. The main section sequence and much of the existing narrative remain.

P2.justification: v4 adds ablation and runtime tables, replaces Figure 10’s PCA grid with annotated segmentation-comparison panels, and revises Figure 1’s styling. The first two tables exchange order, retained appendix tables are regrouped, and Figure 11 gains explicit source/license attribution. Most figures and the overall page design remain.

improvement.justification: Table 4 and Figure 10 better establish the roles and failure modes of the revised segmentation components than v2’s aggregate CLIP results and PCA illustration. Expanded implementation instructions and Table 5 improve reproducibility and runtime transparency. These support a net quality gain concentrated in segmentation validation and explanation. Removing the explicit bandwidth-cost caveat weakens qualification somewhat, although tuning remains documented and new failure analyses add useful boundaries.
